name: Erfoud Centre & Souks
hero_subtitle: Date stalls, everyday markets and the quiet pulse of a Tafilalet desert town.

overview.title: The everyday heart of Erfoud
overview.p1: Erfoud's centre is not a polished tourist medina. It is a working desert-edge town: vegetable stalls, cafes and the date sellers that make the Tafilalet famous.
overview.p2: A slow walk through the main streets shows the real pace of the region. Pair it with a fossil workshop for a solid half-day in town.
overview.p3: Mornings are best for market activity; late afternoon light is kinder when the heat drops.

1.title: How to explore
1.desc: Walk the main streets from your hotel; a short taxi helps if you stay on the outskirts.

2.title: Photos and respect
2.desc: Ask before photographing people in the market. Streets are daily life, not a stage.

3.title: Half-day plan
3.desc: Centre, fossil workshop and date shopping form a natural sequence before a rest.

q1.question: Is there a historic walled medina?
q1.answer: Erfoud is more a modern desert-town centre than a walled imperial medina. Come for atmosphere and markets.

q2.question: Is it safe to walk?
q2.answer: Yes in the daytime centre. Normal awareness applies in the evening.

q3.question: How long do I need?
q3.answer: One to two hours for a first feel; more if you stop for tea and shopping.

q4.question: Best souvenirs?
q4.answer: Dates, small polished fossil pieces from reputable workshops, and simple local crafts.

q5.question: What to combine it with?
q5.answer: A fossil atelier in town and a look at the Ziz palm edges the same half-day.
